html:
Luxembourg is a small country between France, Germany and Belgium, built around a rock fortress. The map shows it from 1650 to 1800, when it was one of the provinces of the southern Netherlands. On the 1650 and 1700 maps the shape is drawn much larger than the duchy was.

Its story begins in 963, when Count Siegfried acquired the castle on the rock. In the 1300s its counts became one of the great families of the Holy Roman Empire: Henry VII and Charles IV were emperors, and in 1354 Luxembourg became a duchy. In 1443 it passed to the dukes of Burgundy and then to the Habsburgs, and it was part of the Habsburg Netherlands and later the Austrian Netherlands.

Its fortress was one of the strongest in Europe; the French engineer Vauban rebuilt it during a French occupation in the 1680s. France annexed it in 1795. The Congress of Vienna made it a grand duchy under the Dutch king in 1815, and in 1839 it lost its western, French-speaking half to Belgium. It was a founding member of the European Union.
